key_insight: The paper introduces two Lean 4 quantum theorem benchmarks and shows that library-augmented agents prove more theorems more reliably than task-only agents.
engineering_relevance: It provides a reproducible way to measure and improve AI proof agents for quantum algorithms and quantum information, with direct implications for verified scientific automation.
method: Built Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench (36 tasks) and Lean-QIT-Bench (40 tasks) for theorem completion.
Evaluated GPT-5.5, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, and MiniMax M3 in a common proving framework.
Compared task-only prompting against library-augmented deduction (LAD) using a verified domain library.
evidence_signal: All tasks compile in a fixed environment and are scored by deterministic proof checking plus targeted semantic review; LAD improved score and completion rate in all 8 model-benchmark comparisons, with top weighted scores of 60.4 and 59.6.
watch_item: The benchmarks are domain-specific and still expose weaknesses in simulation, learning, information measures, and entanglement proofs, so results may not transfer to broader theorem-proving settings.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
